message.content:
The Battle of Waterloo (18 June 1815) was one of the bloodiest single-day engagements of the Napoleonic Wars.  In total, roughly **47,000 soldiers** were killed, wounded, or taken prisoner:

| Side | Approximate casualties |
|------|------------------------|
| French & allied (Bourbon & German) | ~25 000 |
| Anglo‑Dutch & Prussian coalition | ~22 000 |

These figures come from the standard historical consensus (e.g., *The Waterloo Companion* and the *Oxford History of the French Revolution*).  The numbers vary slightly among sources, but the combined total is generally accepted to be around **45 – 50 thousand**.
